title: The Concept of God in Islam (Tawhid)
description: The foundational belief in the absolute oneness of God. Tawhid is the first and most essential principle of Islamic faith — understanding who God is and why monotheism is central to everything else in Islam.

resource.title: Tawhid: The Concept of God in Islam

evidence.summary: Declares the absolute oneness, uniqueness, and eternal nature of God, who neither begets nor is begotten.
Establishes that the absolute first step in calling others to Islam is to believe in the oneness of Allah.

title: The Six Articles of Faith
description: Islam's core beliefs: God, Angels, Holy Books, Prophets, the Day of Judgment, and Divine Decree. These six pillars form the doctrinal backbone of Islamic belief.

resource.title: The Six Pillars of Faith Explained

evidence.summary: Affirms that faith requires believing in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers without distinction.
The Prophet defines Iman (faith) as belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree (Qadar).

title: Understanding Prophethood (Nubuwwah)
description: Why did God send prophets? Learn the Islamic understanding of prophethood — its necessity, characteristics of prophets, and the chain of messengers from Adam to Muhammad.

evidence.summary: States that Allah sent a messenger to every nation to call them to worship Him alone and avoid false gods.
Clarifies that all prophets share the same core message and theological brotherhood, despite differing law details.

title: The Quran: Revelation & Structure
description: How the Quran was revealed over 23 years, its structural organisation into surahs and ayahs, and how to approach reading it for the first time.

evidence.summary: Introduces the Quran as the divine book free of doubt, serving as a guide for the God-conscious.
Encourages the study and teaching of the Quran, designating those who do so as the best of the community.

title: Preservation & Authenticity of the Quran
description: The chain of oral and written transmission that preserved the Quran unchanged for 1,400 years — understanding why Muslims regard the Quran as the literal word of God.

evidence.summary: Expresses Allah's divine guarantee to preserve the Quran from any alteration or loss.
Details the systematic, multi-witness verification process used to compile the Quran into a single volume under Abu Bakr.

title: The Life of the Prophet Muhammad (Overview)
description: A concise biography of the Prophet — his birth in Mecca, his character before revelation, the first revelation, and his significance in Islamic faith.

evidence.summary: Establishes the life and character of the Prophet Muhammad as an excellent pattern of conduct for believers.
The Prophet mentions that he was sent from the best generations of Adam's descendants.

title: The Meccan Period: Early Islam
description: The first 13 years of Islam in Mecca — the early converts, persecution, the Hijra to Abyssinia, and the years before migration to Madinah.

resource.title: When the Moon Split — Meccan Period

title: The Madinan Period: Building a Community
description: The migration to Madinah, the Constitution of Madinah, early battles, and the establishment of the first Islamic state — how the Prophet built a just society.

title: The Five Pillars of Islam
description: The five foundational acts of worship that structure a Muslim's life: Shahada (declaration of faith), Salah (prayer), Zakat (charity), Sawm (fasting), and Hajj (pilgrimage).

evidence.summary: Describes the believers as those who establish prayer and give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger.
The Prophet states that Islam is built on five pillars.

title: The Shahada: Declaration of Faith
description: The meaning of 'La ilaha illallah Muhammadur rasulullah' — what it requires of you, what it denies, and its transformation of a person's life and identity.

evidence.summary: Affirms that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, witnessed by Allah Himself, the angels, and people of knowledge.
Connects acceptance into Islam with declaring that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger.

title: How to Pray (Salah) — Basics
description: A step-by-step guide to performing the five daily prayers: ritual purity (wudu), the direction of prayer (qibla), postures (raka'at), and what to recite.

evidence.summary: Command from Allah to establish prayer specifically for His remembrance.
The Prophet instructs the companions to pray exactly as they have seen him praying.

title: Ritual Purity (Taharah & Wudu)
description: The Islamic concept of purity — physical and ritual. Covers wudu (ablution), ghusl (full bath), and tayammum (dry purification). Required knowledge before performing salah.

evidence.summary: Lays down the detailed obligations for performing wudu (ablution) and ghusl (purification bath) before standing for prayer.
The Prophet declares that ritual purity is half of faith.

title: The Inner Dimension of Prayer (Khushu)
description: Beyond the mechanics — how to achieve presence, focus, and humility in salah. The Prophet described prayer as the pillar of the religion and a conversation with God.

title: Zakat: Obligatory Charity
description: The third pillar — what Zakat is, who pays it, how it is calculated, who receives it, and its role in building economic justice and community solidarity.

evidence.summary: Establishes Zakat directly alongside prayer as an obligatory practice of faith.
The Prophet instructs that Zakat is an obligation to be taken from the wealthy and returned to the poor.

title: Fasting & Ramadan (Sawm)
description: The purpose and practice of fasting — from fajr to maghrib, the spiritual dimensions of Ramadan, Laylat al-Qadr, and how fasting cultivates taqwa (God-consciousness).

resource.title: Ramadan: A Month of Spiritual Training

evidence.summary: Decrees fasting as an obligation upon believers so that they may attain Taqwa (God-consciousness).
Promises complete forgiveness of past sins for whoever fasts during Ramadan with sincere faith and seeking reward.

title: Hajj: The Pilgrimage to Mecca
description: The fifth pillar — the annual pilgrimage, its rituals (Tawaf, Sa'i, Arafat, Mina), its spiritual significance, and its connection to the Prophet Ibrahim.

evidence.summary: States that pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by all people who are able to undertake the journey.
Highlights that performing Hajj sincerely without sin makes a person return as pure as the day they were born.

title: Understanding the Sunnah & Hadith
description: What the Sunnah is, how hadith were collected and authenticated, and why the Prophet's example (sunnah) is the second primary source of Islamic law alongside the Quran.

evidence.summary: Commands believers to obey Allah, obey the Messenger, and refer all matters of dispute back to them.
The Prophet states that all of his followers will enter Paradise except those who refuse by disobeying him.

title: Introduction to Islamic Law (Shariah & Fiqh)
description: The difference between Shariah (divine law) and Fiqh (human legal interpretation). The four major Sunni schools of law and how Muslims navigate legal questions.

title: Halal & Haram: Lawful and Unlawful
description: The Islamic framework for permissibility — covering food, finance, relationships, and conduct. How scholars derive rulings, and why the categories exist.

resource.title: The Lawful and Prohibited in Islam

title: Iman, Islam & Ihsan: Three Levels of Deen
description: The famous hadith of Jibreel explains the three dimensions of the religion: Islam (submission), Iman (belief), and Ihsan (excellence / worshipping as if you see God). A framework for the entire spiritual path.

resource.title: Hadith of Jibreel: Islam, Iman, Ihsan

evidence.summary: Commands justice, goodwill, and Ihsan (excellence / spiritual beauty) in all aspects of life.
The Prophet defines the three dimensions of the Deen: Islam, Iman, and Ihsan.

title: Reading Arabic Script (Letters & Sounds)
description: An introduction to the 28 Arabic letters, their forms, basic pronunciation, and how to connect them. A foundational step toward reading the Quran in its original language.

title: Tajweed: Rules of Quranic Recitation
description: The science of reciting the Quran with correct pronunciation, elongation (madd), and articulation points. Tajweed honors the Quran as it was revealed through the Prophet.

title: Thematic Study: Quran on God, Humanity & Purpose
description: A thematic reading of key Quranic chapters — Surah Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah opening, Surah Al-Ikhlas, and Surah Al-Mulk — exploring the Quran's core messages about existence and meaning.

title: Remembrance of God (Dhikr) & Supplication (Dua)
description: The Prophetic practice of dhikr (remembrance) and dua (supplication) — morning and evening adhkar, the etiquette of dua, and how regular remembrance strengthens the heart.

title: Angels & the Unseen World (Al-Ghayb)
description: The Islamic worldview of the unseen — angels (their nature, roles, and names), jinn, and the Day of Judgment. Faith in the unseen (iman bil-ghayb) is a distinguishing feature of Islamic belief.

title: Death, the Grave & the Afterlife (Akhirah)
description: The Islamic understanding of what happens after death — the barzakh (intermediate state), the resurrection, judgment, and the Quranic descriptions of Jannah (paradise) and Jahannam.

title: Divine Decree (Qadr) & Free Will
description: The sixth article of faith — how Islam reconciles God's complete knowledge and decree with human free will and moral responsibility. A topic many new Muslims find difficult and important.

title: Islamic Character & Ethics (Akhlaq)
description: The Prophet said 'I was sent to perfect good character.' This module covers the Quranic and Prophetic emphasis on character — honesty, compassion, patience, and the ethics of daily Muslim life.

title: Patience (Sabr) & Gratitude (Shukr)
description: Two of the most praised spiritual qualities in the Quran — the art of patient endurance in hardship and sincere gratitude in blessings. Practical tools for the new Muslim navigating a changed life.

title: Dealing with Doubts & Building Certainty (Yaqeen)
description: Practical and spiritual guidance for new Muslims navigating intellectual doubts, wavering faith, and external challenges. How certainty (yaqeen) grows through knowledge, worship, and community.

resource.title: Fortifying Faith in Times of Doubt

title: The Muslim Ummah & Finding Community
description: The concept of the global Muslim community (ummah), the role of the mosque (masjid), and practical guidance for new Muslims on connecting with local communities, Islamic centers, and support networks.

title: The Five Prayer Times & the Call to Prayer
description: Understanding the five prayer windows (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha), how they are determined, the adhan (call to prayer) and its response, and integrating prayer times into daily life.

title: Jumu'ah: The Friday Prayer
description: The significance of Friday in Islam, the obligation of Jumu'ah prayer for men, the khutbah (sermon), and the virtues of Friday as the 'master of days.' An important weekly community anchor.

title: The Islamic (Hijri) Calendar & Key Dates
description: The lunar Islamic calendar — how it works, why it starts from the Hijra, and the significance of key months: Ramadan, Dhul-Hijja, Muharram. Gives cultural orientation to the Muslim year.

title: The Companions of the Prophet (Sahabah)
description: Who the sahabah were, their relationship with the Prophet, key figures (Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Khadijah, Aisha), and why their lives are models for Muslims.

resource.title: Men and Women Around the Messenger

title: Islamic Civilisation: A Brief Overview
description: From the early caliphates to the golden age of Islamic scholarship in Baghdad, Cordoba, and Cairo — how the early Muslim community built one of history's great civilisations.

title: Repentance (Tawbah) & God's Mercy
description: The Islamic theology of repentance — God's infinite mercy, the conditions for valid tawbah, and how the door of repentance is always open. Critical for new Muslims overcoming guilt from the past.

resource.title: The Concept of Repentance in Islam

title: Spiritual Excellence & Ihsan in Daily Life
description: Translating the concept of Ihsan (doing what is beautiful / worshipping as if you see God) into daily practice — in worship, dealings, speech, and relationships.

resource.title: The Inner Dimensions of Islamic Worship

title: Introduction to Quranic Tafsir (Exegesis)
description: What tafsir is and why it matters — how scholars interpret the Quran, the different tafsir methodologies (classical, thematic, scientific), and recommended tafsir resources for English speakers.

title: Advanced Fiqh of Worship
description: A deeper look at the fiqh rulings governing salah, zakat, fasting, and hajj — including missed prayers, prayer while travelling, and common questions new Muslims face.

title: Muslim Identity as a Revert: Navigating Change
description: A pastoral and practical guide specifically for reverts — navigating family reactions, cultural adjustments, name changes, halal lifestyle challenges, and building an authentic Muslim identity.
